officialDocs.label: Jira scopes for OAuth 2.0 (3LO) and Forge

verdict.summary: An OAuth 2.0 (3LO) integration is self-serve: create it in the developer console, toggle sharing, and any Atlassian user can authorize it the same day, though unapproved apps show a 'not reviewed by Atlassian' warning. The real constraint for an agent is rate limits enforced since March 2026: by default your app shares one 65,000-point hourly quota across all customer sites, and a per-tenant quota needs Atlassian review.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Create the integration, add Jira/Confluence APIs and scopes on Permissions, set a callback URL, run the code flow, then call accessible-resources to get the cloudid.

timeToProd.assumes: A shared 3LO integration that reads and writes Jira/Confluence data; sharing alone is same day with a warning, and the upper bound covers Atlassian approval to remove the warning and a per-tenant rate-limit pool.
timeToProd.waitingOn: Nothing to go live. Optionally, Atlassian app approval (a staff post cited a 10-business-day objective) and review for the per-tenant rate-limit pool.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Sharing needs no review per the docs. The approval timing is from a community post and may be outdated; Atlassian publishes no review SLA for 3LO apps or the per-tenant pool.

prerequisites.item: An Atlassian account and an Atlassian Cloud site (a free Jira/Confluence site works) for testing
prerequisites.why: The consent screen makes the user pick a site, and API calls are made against that site's cloudid.

prerequisites.item: A single distributable app for all customers, not one 3LO app per customer and not customer-generated API tokens
prerequisites.why: Atlassian's June 2025 guidance says per-customer 3LO apps and stored customer API tokens violate its standards, and non-compliant apps may lose platform access.

prerequisites.item: A decision between OAuth 2.0 (3LO), Forge and Connect
prerequisites.why: 3LO is hosted by you and suits accessing data on behalf of a user from an external service. Forge is Atlassian-hosted, installed by site admins, and the only type accepted for new Marketplace submissions since Sep 17, 2025. Connect is legacy and not recommended for new apps.

prerequisites.item: A test instance of your product for reviewers, if you seek approval or a listing
prerequisites.why: Marketplace reviewers need to run through setup and configuration.

scopeTiers.impact: offline_access is needed for a refresh token. Identity scopes come from the User identity API.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Scopes observed in the live OIDC discovery document.

scopeTiers.impact: Enough for an agent that searches, reads and edits issues and pages. Atlassian says to use classic scopes when available. The user's own Jira/Confluence permissions still constrain the app.
Use only when a classic scope doesn't cover the API. Atlassian recommends fewer than 50 scopes per app, and adding scopes forces existing users to re-consent.
Calls only succeed for users with the matching Jira admin permissions.

steps.title: Choose 3LO vs Forge
steps.detail: For an external agent acting on behalf of users, pick an OAuth 2.0 (3LO) integration. Choose Forge instead if you need in-product UI, admin-level installs or a Marketplace listing.

steps.title: Create the OAuth 2.0 integration
steps.detail: In the developer console choose Create > OAuth 2.0 integration and pick a grant type: account-level (can cover multiple sites) or resource-level (limited to the sites the user picks).

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The console URL returned HTTP 200 on 2026-10-20; we did not sign in.

steps.title: Add APIs and scopes on Permissions
steps.detail: Add the Jira and/or Confluence API, then the classic scopes the agent needs. Set the callback URL under Authorization.

steps.title: Implement the authorization code flow
steps.detail: Redirect to https://auth.atlassian.com/authorize?audience=api.atlassian.com&client_id=...&scope=read:jira-work%20offline_access&redirect_uri=...&state=...&response_type=code&prompt=consent. Exchange at POST https://auth.atlassian.com/oauth/token. PKCE S256 is supported.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: PKCE support observed in the live discovery document.

steps.title: Resolve the cloudid and call the APIs
steps.detail: GET https://api.atlassian.com/oauth/token/accessible-resources, then call https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/{cloudid}/rest/api/3/... or /ex/confluence/{cloudid}/.... Infer the product from each resource's scopes, since ids aren't unique across containers.

steps.title: Handle rotating refresh tokens
steps.detail: Store the new refresh token after every refresh. Rotating tokens expire after 90 days of inactivity, and an old token can be reused for 10 minutes. invalid_grant 'Unknown or invalid refresh token' means re-authorize.

steps.title: Design for the points-based rate limits
steps.detail: Budget against the default Global Pool of 65,000 points/hour shared across all tenants. Read RateLimit-Reason and Retry-After, pause on quota errors, and back off with jitter on burst errors.

steps.title: Enable sharing
steps.detail: Under Distribution toggle Enable sharing. The app is private by default, so only you can authorize it until then. No review is required to share.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Distribution may also ask for a personal data declaration; we couldn't confirm the current form fields.

steps.title: Optional: request app approval to remove the warning
steps.detail: Unapproved integrations show users a 'not yet reviewed by Atlassian' warning. Approval follows the third-party integration listing process, and a Marketplace listing isn't needed to submit.

steps.title: Atlassian approval review
steps.detail: A Marketplace team member reviews and may test against your instance. An Atlassian staff member cited a 10-business-day objective in 2025.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: Community forum statement, not official policy.

steps.title: Request the per-tenant rate-limit pool when scaling
steps.detail: The Per-Tenant Pool gives a separate hourly quota per customer site (scaled by edition and user count, up to 500,000 points/hour) and is assigned only after Atlassian review.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The request process and timing weren't documented on the page.

agentCanDo: Choose between 3LO and Forge and pick classic scopes
Implement the code flow with prompt=consent, PKCE and offline_access
Resolve cloudids via accessible-resources and route Jira vs Confluence calls
Build rotating refresh-token storage and points-aware rate limiting
Draft the approval/listing description and reviewer test instructions
humanMustDo: Sign in to the developer console and create the integration
Add APIs, scopes and the callback URL, then enable sharing
Submit for approval and give reviewers a test instance
Request the per-tenant rate-limit pool from Atlassian when scaling

blockers.symptom: Users see a warning that the app has not yet been reviewed by Atlassian
blockers.cause: The integration is shared but not approved.
blockers.fix: Submit it for approval through the third-party integration process; a Marketplace listing isn't required.

blockers.symptom: HTTP 429 with RateLimit-Reason: jira-quota-global-based across many customers at once
blockers.cause: The default Global Pool shares 65,000 points/hour across all tenants of your app, enforced since March 2, 2026.
blockers.fix: Pause until reset, cut object-heavy reads, and request the Per-Tenant Pool via Atlassian review.

blockers.symptom: Outside users can't authorize; only the developer can
blockers.fix: Enable sharing under Distribution in the developer console.

blockers.cause: The refresh token expired (90 days inactive), the user changed their password, or the app didn't store the rotated token.
blockers.fix: Persist each new refresh token; on this error send the user through authorization again.

blockers.symptom: Agent only sees one site when the customer has several
blockers.cause: The consent screen makes the user pick one site per authorization.
blockers.fix: Have users repeat the flow per site, or use an account-level grant type where available.

blockers.symptom: Existing users lose access or are prompted again after you change scopes
blockers.cause: Adding or removing scopes requires users who previously consented to re-consent.
blockers.fix: Settle scopes before sharing and batch scope changes.

nuances.text: 3LO apps are installed per user, not per site. A site admin can't restrict an individual user's access except by uninstalling the app.

Atlassian's docs conflict on listings: the platform overview says 3LO integrations can't be listed on the Marketplace, while the 3LO guide says they can have informational listings with limited features.
Connect is legacy: since Sep 17, 2025 only Forge apps can be submitted to the Marketplace, and new extensibility features ship only on Forge.
Rate-limit costs are per object returned (e.g. users cost 2 points, issues 1) plus 1 base point per request, so large JQL searches burn quota fast.
Asking customers to generate and paste API tokens for your service to store is a policy violation per Atlassian's 2025 guidance, so 3LO or Forge is the sanctioned path.
The authorization server publishes OIDC discovery with PKCE (S256), a device authorization endpoint and a revocation endpoint.
